legend: G-banded karyogram: 46,XY,t(8;9)(p22;p24.1) (<<36735>>). A PCM1::JAK2 rearrangement was confirmed by FISH and by RT-PCR; the abnormal chromosomes 8 and 9 are depicted to the right of their corresponding normal chromosomes (<<36736>>).

G-banded karyogram: 46,XY,t(8;9)(p22;p24.1) (<<36735>>). A PCM1::JAK2 rearrangement was confirmed by FISH and by RT-PCR; the abnormal chromosomes 8 and 9 are depicted to the right of their corresponding normal chromosomes (<<36736>>).

G-banded karyogram: 45,X,-Y,t(9;22)(p13;q11.2). A BCR::JAK2 rearrangement was demonstrated by RT-PCR. JAK2 is located on the short arm of chromosome 9, in chromosomal band 9p24 on the + strand, and BCR is located on the long arm of chromosome 22, in chromosomal band 22q11.2 on the + strand. Because of the localization of both genes on the + strand and on the p-arm (JAK2) and q-arm (BCR), a simple reciprocal translocation cannot result in a functional fusion gene; a second rearrangement is required: in this case an inversion within the short arm of chromosome 9 translocated to the long arm of chromosome 22 – inv(9)(p24.1p13) – which is cytogenetically not visible.

A representative interphase nucleus with an abnormal JAK2 (9p24.1) rearrangement signal pattern (one intact fusion signal, and separated red and green signals indicating a disruption), using a JAK2 break-apart probe. A normal nucleus is also present, with a normal JAK2 signal pattern (two intact fusion signals).
